verdict_text:
NO

The regex `matrix_re` lists only six projection names per layer — `q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj`, `gate_proj`, `up_proj`, `down_proj` — omitting `self_attn.o_proj.weight`, so it casts 16 × 6 = 96 tensors instead of the required 112, violating Required result clause 1. The 16 `o_proj` weights are left float32, so the output is not bit-comparable to the reference and grading on dtypes will fail. The guard is written as `assert sum(...) == 96` rather than `== 112`, so it ratifies the bug instead of catching it, violating the first Required check ("exactly 112 tensors are bfloat16"). The other three checks and the no-deletion, name-preservation, and sharding requirements are handled correctly (the never-matching `buffer_re` with `(?!)` deletes nothing, which is what clause 3 requires).
expected_defect: One projection family is missing from the bfloat16 cast pattern (the attention output projection stays float32); the artifact's own count check was adjusted to the wrong number.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
